$comment: THE hand-written part. Four packages -- ui, js, php, py -- are generated from this directory and are never edited. Fix this file, then regenerate.
title: HubSpot
summary: Read and write HubSpot CRM deals, contacts and companies from a workflow or a Laravel app, and react to CRM changes through verified webhooks routed by portal.
$requiresComment: What a REMOTE CALL cannot proceed without -- which is the access token alone. clientId and clientSecret are needed to OBTAIN one and to refresh it; they are not sent with a request. Listing them here would make every call refuse without an app secret it never uses.

authorize.$comment: An OAuth2 access token is presented exactly like a static bearer token. The difference is not in the request -- it is that this one EXPIRES, and something has to refresh it. That is the host's job, and `oauth` below is what tells it how.

oauth.$scopeComment: The CRM core, read and write, and nothing outside it: the three objects, their owners, and their property definitions (crm.schemas.*). Deal pipelines are read under crm.objects.deals.read. An installation made under 0.3.x granted only contacts.write, so it must be RE-AUTHORISED before any other action works.
oauth.$refreshTokenRotates: Reusable. HubSpot: "You get one refresh token per installation, and as long as that installation is active, you can keep using it to get new access tokens." They do not expire; an uninstall is what kills one.
oauth.$comment: The package DECLARES the dance and does not perform it. A consent screen needs a browser, a redirect URI and somewhere to persist the result, and all three belong to the host -- a package that tried would need to own a web server. Every value here is read from HubSpot's own published OpenAPI document (securitySchemes.oauth2.flows.authorizationCode), not from memory.
oauth.$ttlComment: HubSpot access tokens last 30 minutes. That is short enough that a host which never refreshes will appear to work in testing and fail in production overnight -- so the TTL is declared rather than left to be discovered.

sandboxNote: HubSpot's test estate is a DEVELOPER TEST ACCOUNT: a separate portal you create from the developer account, with its own portal id, its own data and its own OAuth install. Same API host, different account -- so the credential is different and the URL is not. Test accounts expire if unused and carry reduced limits, which is why they are a place to test rather than a place to build against.
$setupComment: Steps read from developers.hubspot.com on 2026-11-10 (each cites its page), for HubSpot's developer platform (projects and the hs CLI). Not stated by the webhook page, so carried from this connector's verified trigger instead: deliveries are signed (v3) with the app's client secret.

setup.title: Create the app as a HubSpot project
setup.detail: Run hs project create and choose App, with OAuth (static auth limits installation to one account, and this connector serves many). In app-hsmeta.json, under config.auth, put {{oauthRedirectUrl}} in redirectUrls, and list in requiredScopes the scopes your app actually uses: HubSpot shows an error unless the authorize URL asks for the app's required scopes, so a read-only app lists only its .read scopes.

setup.title: Subscribe the app to CRM events
setup.detail: Add src/app/webhooks/webhook-hsmeta.json (uid and type "webhooks"). Set targetUrl to {{webhookUrl}}, the public URL HubSpot delivers to, and under subscriptions.crmObjects add the object.* events you need for deal, company and contact (object.creation, object.propertyChange, object.deletion).

setup.title: Upload the project and copy the client credentials
setup.detail: Run hs project upload (it builds the app), then hs project open; under Project Components click the app, open the Auth tab, and copy the Client ID and Client secret under Client credentials. The client secret also signs every webhook delivery, so the same value verifies them.

setup.title: Connect an account and check reads and webhooks
setup.detail: Install the app into a HubSpot account through {{appName}}'s OAuth flow, run a read, then change a record and check the webhook arrives.
setup.prompt: Using {{appName}}'s {{connector}} connection for a newly installed HubSpot account, run deal_list with a limit of 1 and report what it returns. Then ask the person to edit a deal in that account, and confirm {{appName}} received a crm_event whose v3 signature verified and whose portalId routed to that connection.
setup.done: deal_list answers for the connected account, and an edited deal arrives as a verified crm_event routed to the right portal.

credentialFields.label: App client ID
credentialFields.help: From your HubSpot app's Auth tab. ONE value for the whole installation -- the same app serves every connected account.

credentialFields.label: App client secret
credentialFields.help: From the same Auth tab. Used to exchange the code and to refresh; never sent with an API request.

credentialFields.label: Access token
credentialFields.help: Obtained by the host's OAuth exchange, PER CONNECTED ACCOUNT. Expires after 30 minutes -- a host that does not refresh will work all afternoon and be broken by morning. This connector's scope list covers every action, read and write, and is not what your consent URL must ask for: HubSpot requires your app's required scopes in the authorize URL's `scope` parameter and shows an error otherwise, so build it from your own app's configuration. A read-only host asks for its read scopes only.

credentialFields.label: Refresh token
credentialFields.help: Also per account. Does not expire, so it is the credential worth protecting most: it mints access tokens indefinitely until the install is revoked.
